quest.title: To Reclaim an Ancient Name
quest.description: To rescue Kachina, who has been trapped in the Night Kingdom, you must first seek out her Ancient Name. Kinich says that he has given the ritual implements needed to do so to the Chief of the Scions of the Canopy. Head there and ask around.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.title: Black Stone Under a White Stone

talks.objective: Pay the Scions of the Canopy a visit

dialogues.speaker: Amauta
dialogues.text: Anything else I can get you?

talks.objective: Talk to the Chief of the tribe, Wayna

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Chasca?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Nice to see you again, Wayna.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'm afraid we don't have time for pleasantries, so I'll get right to it. We're here for the Spiritspeaker Stone.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Whoa, hold on a second. At least tell me why you need it, first.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: My friend, Kachina, is trapped within the Night Kingdom. We need the Stone to find her Ancient Name and rescue her.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Rescue her? From the Night Kingdom?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but someone needs to tell you what you don't want to hear. Going there... A "mature warrior" would never make such a foolish decision.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: The nature of battle is unpredictable. You never know how it's going to end. Losing a friend is tragic, but when that happens, the best thing you can do is focus on how to prevent further casualties...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I appreciate what you're trying to say, Chief Wayna, but if the price of "maturity" is abandoning a friend in need, I'll choose foolishness any day. If Kachina's still holding on, then so will I.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: I thought you might say that... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Is something wrong, Wayna? This doesn't seem like you.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: "Life isn't complete without taking risks" — that's always been your mantra.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Haha... It's nothing. The Night Kingdom is a dangerous place. Can't blame me for checking if you were up to the task.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: If you're that determined, far be it from me to stop you. Here's the stone. Keep it safe, okay? It's not like we have a spare.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, seems like you two go way back... But, aren't you from the Flower-Feather Clan, Chasca?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Oh, Chasca's a peacemaker, so she's famous throughout the tribes. She's always the one people call to resolve conflicts, so we slowly got to know each other that way.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Her younger sister, Chuychu's always hanging around our tribe, too. She's helped us out a lot in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you have a younger sister!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yes... I'll introduce you to her sometime.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But, let's get back to business. Wayna, how do we use the Stone?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: As you probably know, your intended destination is completely different from the real world. The Night Kingdom is like a river flowing with "concepts," and the Ancient Name you seek is like a tiny fish swimming downstream.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: In that sense, the Stone is like a fishing boat drifting down the river. But, the boat alone isn't enough. You need a "fisherman" experienced enough to steer it in the right direction.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We couldn't do that ourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: With a little practice, I'm sure you could. You have the strength and the talent... If you want to make sure this works, though, I could recommend someone to you.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Who?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Vichama — a legendary warrior and scout from our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: He's got a keen eye and a well-honed intuition. Even his Ancient Name means "to seek"... If you're "fishing" for a Name, you're gonna want him on the boat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Vichama? Why does that name sound familiar...?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: He's one of Auntie Atea's "hot spring buddies." I've heard stories about him.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Where can we find him?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Ever since Mallko passed, he spends most of his time gazing out at the scenery from the clifftops. Follow the path that way, and I'm sure you'll find him.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Thank you. We'll go look for him there.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Good luck. I hope everything goes well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Someone admiring the scenery from the clifftops... Ah, that must be him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello there! Are you Vichama?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: That's me. Did you need something?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell him about Kachina and the Spiritspeaker Stone...

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: What? You're saying... you can bring someone back from the Night Kingdom? How is that even possible?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: No, if you really think about it... Anything's possible in that kind of place. But, that would mean...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Are you okay? You don't look so good...

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Everything's fine.... I'll help you, but I do have a small request.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: After I help you find Kachina's Ancient Name, I want to use the Stone to look for my friend's as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your friend? Oh, Wayna mentioned someone named "Mallko." Is that who you're talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Yes, but I'd rather not get into it, if it's all the same to you.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: That's not a problem. We agree to your request.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yeah! Since you're helping us find Kachina's Ancient Name, it's only right that we return the favor!

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Then we're agreed. Can I have a look at the Stone?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: ...I see. From what I can tell, it functions almost like an Abyssal Pylon — both connect the Night Kingdom to the living world.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Once the connection is established, the Abyss will come surging through the opening like a predator honing in on the scent of blood. So, we have to be sure not to use it in a tribal settlement.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you got all that just from looking at it?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I just picked up on the basics, really. I still have no idea why it works. You said someone named Citlali invented this? They must be a genius.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I'll go find an open area and start setting things up. In the meantime, I need you to get two things for me.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We'll go right away! What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: First, I'll need some hook-ropes. Pretty much every store around here carries them, so no need to go anywhere special. Oh, and I need to build a "net" out of them, so make sure you get a good amount.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Wait, are you saying you're going to use a real net to "catch" Kachina's Ancient Name? How does that work when one's tangible and one's not?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: By creating something tangible in our world — like a net — we can create a connection to a corresponding "concept" in the Night Kingdom. Basically, I'm going to use the "concept of a net" to catch something equally intangible — an Ancient Name.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, I see. What about the second thing you needed?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Right, I need one... no, two chunks of Obsidian. Once we bring the Ancient Names into our world, we'll need a place to store them.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Normally, you can only get Obsidian from the Children of Echoes, but I heard there's a traveling merchant from that tribe around here somewhere, so maybe you can try your luck there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gotcha!

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Alright, let's split up. See that clearing? Let's meet over there when you're done.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Oh, and, you can send someone with me, if you want. In case you're worried I might take the Stone for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: ...What do you think, Chasca?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: There's no need. Wayna spoke highly of you. That means you're trustworthy.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I appreciate it... even though that doesn't mean much to me anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Anyway, it'll take some time to set everything up, so no need to rush. I'll see you in a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What an odd guy. He seemed so defeated, but also really invested in the Stone at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I don't have any more insight than you, Paimon. Let's just focus on the preparations for now.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hang on Kachina... We're coming for you.

talks.objective: Make preparations to seek the Ancient Name (0/2)

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hello. Do you have any hook-ropes for sale?

dialogues.speaker: Amauta
dialogues.text: Hook-ropes? As in rock climbing equipment?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yes. How much for your whole stock?

dialogues.speaker: Amauta
dialogues.text: The whole thing? Let me see... That would be 30,000 Mora in total. Deal?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Deal.

dialogues.speaker: Amauta
dialogues.text: Wait, really?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: What, you want me to drive down the price? We just need these as fast as possible. Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Amauta
dialogues.text: No problem at all! I'll even pass along some information on the house. These ropes are usually used by rock climbing enthusiasts. If you want to learn, Roca's the person you want to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Amauta
dialogues.text: Alright, that's everything. Here you go.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Now, we need the Obsidian. Let's go talk to the Traveling Merchant Vichama mentioned.

talks.objective: Make preparations to seek the Ancient Name (1/2)

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Excuse me, do you sell Obsidian?

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: Why, yes! I've got a chunk for sale right over there.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Perfect! Is that the only one, though? We actually need two.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: Hmm, that might be tough. Tell you what, I'll take a look through these boxes over here, and we'll see what we can find.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Thank you so much. We'll wait here.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Relax. Everything's going according to plan.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I know... It's just, I could tell Vichama feels the same way about his friend that I do about Kachina. I hope this chunk of Obsidian isn't the only one...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Kachina always carries all sorts of shiny stones with her. If I was the one trapped in the Night Kingdom, she'd have a whole pile of Obsidian ready in a heartbeat.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: Well, would you look at that, I did bring an extra... Here you go, young lady. How does it look?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Perfect! Thank you! How much do I owe you?

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: If you hadn't shown up, these stones would have just sat here collecting dust. I'll take 3,000 Mora for both.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: Here you go... By the way, I heard you mention Vichama just now. You running an errand for him, then?

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: How's he doing? Mallko's been gone for five years, now. It's about time he started to move forward.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you know what happened between them?

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: I heard about it in passing while I was out drinking one night, but I don't know all the details. Vichama and Mallko grew up together and even made a name for themselves together.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: Mallko was an amazing fighter, capable of knocking out multiple opponents in a single hit, while Vichama excelled at scouting and analyzing the battlefield. The two made an excellent team, and managed to beat back the Abyss several times.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: Five years ago, they both emerged triumphant in the Pilgrimage and were placed on the same team to fight the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: But on the eve of battle, the Abyss launched an attack on their tribe, and Vichama suffered an injury to his leg while attempting to rescue someone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: The team agreed that he couldn't go fight the Abyss in his condition.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: Vichama didn't argue. He knew going to the front lines with an injured leg would make him a burden in battle. So, they raised the issue with the Pyro Archon, and she agreed to let him stay behind.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: It's just... Mallko and the others ended up facing hordes of Abyssal monsters in numbers that far exceeded anyone's expectations. The team made an error in judgment, and they fell to the onslaught.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: Vichama went into a deep depression after that. He blames himself for everything.

response.speaker: Pajaten
response.text: You're not wrong. But, it's possible he chooses to blame himself, not because he did something wrong, but because he wasn't able to do anything at all.

response.speaker: Pajaten
response.text: I've tried convincing him to move forward, to stop dwelling on the past. But, the shadow of Mallko's death hangs over him still.

response.speaker: Pajaten
response.text: The Abyss has caused so much suffering, and some wounds never heal. I wish there was something he could do to make himself feel better, but... *sigh*

response.speaker: Pajaten
response.text: Anyway, that's the gist of it. Maybe you could help him talk things through sometime. I would really appreciate it.

choices.text: It doesn't sound like it was his fault.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Did you get everything?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yup, it's all here. When do we start?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I've made all the necessary adjustments, so we're good to go.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: As agreed, I'll help you find Kachina's Ancient Name, and then you return the favor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could I ask a question?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Go ahead.

choices.text: Are you seeking your friend's Ancient Name...

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: ...Yes.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: After Mallko fell, I scoured the battlefield to see what happened. It turned out... he wasn't bested by some impossibly powerful foe. He was dragged to his grave by the sheer number of enemies.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: If I had been there, I would've been able to sense the danger. I could've warned them not to advance...

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: I've always blamed myself for what happened... But, when you told me about Kachina, I realized there's a chance Mallko might also be alive, fighting for survival in the Night Kingdom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... that happened several years ago, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Pyro Archon said all life within the Night Kingdom eventually becomes one with the sea of souls...

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: There might not be much hope, but I still have to try. Mallko and I promised each other... Even if we never managed to root out the Abyss for good, we would fight together until the end.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Alright, let's get to it. I'll start searching for the "conceptualized" version of Kachina's Ancient Name. If you see any "fragments" scattered around the area, please collect them.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Make sure you prepare yourselves for battle. As I said, the Stone will link the mortal realm to the Night Kingdom. The Abyss will likely emerge in response.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Vichama spends most of his time up in the clifftops, gazing at the scenery. You should head over there and have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: I hope Vichama can move past this whole thing soon...

dialogues.speaker: Pajaten
dialogues.text: Looking to buy something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Vichama!

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Quick... Take it!

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I found Kachina's Ancient Name... Hang in there, Mallko... Just a little longer...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Something's not right. The power of the Abyss is getting stronger.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: The Abyss is corroding his body! Vichama, you can't keep going, you'll die—

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: ...I should've died five years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I just need a little more time. Please! I'm almost there!

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: This power...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hanging in there?

choices.text: I can't hold them back much longer!

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Mallko... No! Why can't I find him!? Why...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: We can't wait any longer. Pull him away from the Stone, Mualani!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I already tried, but the power of the Abyss has him in a chokehold... It's like he's tied to the Stone with an invisible rope.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: In that case, we have no choice. I'm sorry, Citlali.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Get back.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: ...Chasca? Wait—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ouch... What happened just now? It looked like the Spiritspeaker Stone was—

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: The Stone's power was spiraling out of control. The only way to stop it was to destroy it.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: You were all caught in the shockwave of the explosion. You might feel dizzy for a while, but that's normal.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Give us a heads up next time, will you? You're lucky we managed to dodge in time.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I thought I said to get back...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Yeah, barely a second before you made it go poof! Not everyone has your reflexes, Chasca. We were THIS close to getting dragged into the explosion!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Okay, I'll be more careful next time.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: At least Kachina's Ancient Name is still in one piece... Wait, where's Vichama?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Vichama!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Vichama...

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: I couldn't find Mallko's Ancient Name. It... must be completely gone by now.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Once your Ancient Name disappears, there's no coming back. From the very beginning, I knew there was a slim chance, but still...

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: And, now, it's too late to save him... From the minute he left that day, it was already too late.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Vichama...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I'm sure he's heard enough condolences over the years... Let's just give him some space.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's that in your hands, Vichama? It looks like something's glowing!

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Huh? This is...

response.speaker: Pisac
response.text: Hey, Mallko, got any strength left?

response.speaker: Mallko
response.text: Not enough to swing a sword, but to say a few last words? Sure...

response.speaker: Pisac
response.text: Haha, too bad no one will get to hear them.

response.speaker: Pisac
response.text: I never thought I'd actually die on this mission. *sigh* Not that I'm afraid to die, it's just... hard, thinking about my mom's face when she hears the news...

response.speaker: Mallko
response.text: Guess I have something to be thankful for, then. My parents died a long time ago... They won't have to mourn me.

response.speaker: Mallko
response.text: Pisac? Hah, always had to beat me at everything, didn't you... Right to the end, you never were one for goodbyes.

response.speaker: Mallko
response.text: Maybe you're right, maybe no one will get to hear our last words. But, just in case...

response.speaker: Mallko
response.text: Vichama, I'm so glad you didn't come with us.

response.speaker: Mallko
response.text: Don't be sad. Just keep on living... for the both of us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Was that... a memory?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Seems like we were able to salvage something after all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Feeling any better, Vichama?

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Of course. Seeing him, hearing his voice again... It makes me unbelievably happy.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: ...But, it also brings with it an even deeper pain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A deeper pain? Why?

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Mallko was always the type to put on a brave face, but in that memory just now... his hands were shaking, and his smile was forced.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: For all these years, I regretted not being able to fight alongside him to the end. And now I know... At the end of his life, he was thinking the same thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Vichama...

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: I'm fine... Actually, I heard Chief Wayna wasn't really on board with your plan to go to the Night Kingdom.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: When you asked for my help, I hesitated, too. I knew helping you find your friend's Ancient Name meant leading you one step closer to danger.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: But... I also understood why you had to try. Everyone has regrets in life, but not everyone gets the chance to make up for them.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Once allowed to fester, guilt strips us of our most valuable qualities as warriors. In that sense, we might as well choose the braver path from the very beginning...

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: If I could do it all over again, I would have followed Mallko to the frontlines no matter what. Even with an injured leg, there were still things I could have done.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: That way... even if the outcome stayed the same, I still would have fought alongside him to the end.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: There are critical junctures in life, and if you don't seize the chance to act, there's no going back.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: That's something I had to learn in hindsight, but you're still at the crossroads of your journey, so... I hope you can walk away without regrets.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Thank you, Vichama. I feel even more determined, now. Kachina will come back to us — I'll make sure of it.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I promised I would find her, and I intend to keep that promise.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: That's good to hear. *cough* Strange... My body, it's...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #Once Abyssal corrosion enters the body, a portion will fuse itself to your internal organs. Even though {NICKNAME} possesses powers of purification, the corrosion can never be fully eradicated.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #Thanks to {M#him}{F#her}, though, you were only briefly exposed. Slowing your breathing and controlling your emotions should help you keep the symptoms in check.

response.speaker: Vichama
response.text: Phew... That does make me feel better. You seem very knowledgeable about all this.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Just speaking from experience, that's all.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Anyway, we've recovered Kachina's Ancient Name, so we're off to a great start. Let's get Vichama back to his tribe and tell Wayna the good news.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Oh, um... and apologize for destroying the Spiritspeaker Stone. We had no choice, though, so he'll probably understand... right?

choices.text: I'll help buy you some time.

talks.objective: Return to the Scions of the Canopy

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Chuychu, are you really gonna just stand there like that? I don't know what you want from me...

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: I think you know exactly what I'm trying to say, Uncle Wayna. I can hear it in your voice.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Honestly, it's just one thing after another with you two...

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Ah, they're back.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Chuychu? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Hah, don't play dumb with your own sister! You know exactly why I'm here.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: My apologies, everyone, I just need to borrow Chasca for a few minutes.... You, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I'll be just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who was that?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Chuychu... Chasca's younger sister, although the two aren't actually related by blood. It's kind of a long story...

choices.text: Right! She did call herself Chasca's "sister" just now.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: It's not really my story to tell, but I guess it's not a secret... You see, Chasca was actually raised by Qucusaurs.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: She was afflicted with a rare disease when she was a child and abandoned in the wild as a result. The Abyss found her out there, all on her own, and tried to devour her. But, in the end, all that did was trigger her will to live.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: That strength of will pushed her to survive, but it also planted a seed of "conflict" within her. Eventually, she was adopted by the Qucusaurs. Wherever they went, she followed, getting into fights right and left.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: For some reason, Paimon can totally imagine that...

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: Haha, well, when Chasca finally returned to human society, it was Chuychu's parents who adopted her. At the time, Chasca still had a habit of getting into fights, so Chuychu was always taking her around, apologizing to everyone.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Aww, I remember those days! One of those fights was definitely with me... But, you know kids... You're fighting one minute, and you're friends the next!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Eventually, she found a way to rein in that desire to fight, and now she's who people call to resolve conflicts. She's known as "the Peacemaker."

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: ...It sounds like she still argues with Chuychu, though. Don't siblings usually stop fighting when they get older?

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: *sigh* That's partly my fault. Chuychu asked me to stop Chasca from doing anything dangerous, but you probably know by now, once Chasca makes up her mind, there's no changing it.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Ahh, I get it. No wonder you tried to talk us out of going to the Night Kingdom. Chasca even said that wasn't like you.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: I'm all for your adventure. You need to take risks when you're young, 'cause by the time you're my age, you couldn't attempt something like that even if you wanted to. Better try now than live with regrets later, that's what I say.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: Still, I can understand where Chuychu's coming from. In the end, nobody wants to sit back and let a loved one put their life on the line.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Alright, it's just the two of us now. You have one minute to explain yourself.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I don't have anything to say. You don't have to approve, but you should know I only do what's necessary.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: That attitude is exactly the problem. It's like you don't care! You try to sneak off to the Night Kingdom behind my back, and then play it down, as if it's just a trip abroad.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Well... technically, I am going abroad, right?

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Again with the excuses!

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: We agreed, didn't we? There are four levels of danger. If it's not something urgent, you can only engage in level 2 danger and below. You can only go up to level 3 if a situation is so dire, there's absolutely no alternative.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: But, a trip to the Night Kingdom? If that's not a level 4, I don't know what is. And you were just going to sneak into the place without saying anything!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: What do you mean, sneak into the place? I always planned on walking in there with my head held high.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: You bought off Uncle Wayna, didn't you? He promised me he'd stop you from doing anything dangerous. It's like he didn't even try!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: You feel like he went back on his word? What if I told you my mind was made up, and there was nothing he could have done — not even by force?

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: I knew it! So he did try to say something, but you didn't listen!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: This is important. If you were in my shoes, you'd make the same decision.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: You don't know that. I'm a doctor, and I handle logistics. If you're going to waltz into a dangerous situation where you could lose control at any moment, it's my duty to say something.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Alright, whatever. Anything else?

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: You... What do you mean, "anything else"? Why don't you reflect on what you've done, and promise me you'll stay put.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Time out... Is this one of our normal arguments, or a serious one?

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Chasca, does it sound like I'm joking?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Then, you need to know something. What happened to Kachina was partially my fault. I can't leave her there to die. That's not who I am.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: But, the person you become when you lose control... That's also not who you are!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: That's a different issue. You said it yourself — a person is only as good as their morals. If I want to live in Natlan, I need to display qualities that make me worthy of this nation.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: I've also told you that managing your condition is equally important.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Sometimes, you have to make sacrifices. Alright, let's stop this here. If we keep going, I might actually have to get serious, and I think Wayna prefers his roof attached to his house.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Is that a threat? That sounds like a threat to me.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Chuychu! Younger sisters are supposed to listen to their elders.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: So, you're really going to go? No matter what I say? I'm supposed to be your sister...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Then, support me. I'll be back, all you have to do is wait.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: *sigh*... Chasca...

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: So, that's it... Why'd you have to turn out to be so... darn... annoying!

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: *sigh*... You two are something else...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Something you wanted to say?

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: I know you aren't related by blood, but you two sure are similar.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Really?

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: ...Y'know, I said that very thing to Chuychu not too long ago, and she reacted the exact same way, down to the very tone of voice.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: It's not my place to get involved, but I will say this... Try to spend a little more time with your sister. You're tough kids, but that doesn't mean you have to go it alone.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Thank you.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: Anytime... Alright, if you're done with the Spiritspeaker Stone, you might as well hand it over.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: According to Kinich, it's an important ceremonial artifact, so it'd be safer to keep it with me.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Um, about that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh*... If only Tone-Deaf Bard was here. He could have "repaired" it just like the Holy Lyre...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: The Spiritspeaker Stone might be... two stones now.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You explain the sequence of events to Wayna...

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: I see... *sigh* Sounds like it was an urgent situation. If someone's life was on the line, then you had no choice.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: Still, Citlali's gonna be a nightmare to deal with now that you've broken her stuff. I'll explain everything to her later.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: Stay safe out there in the Night Kingdom, okay? I'll wait here for your safe return.

choices.text: But, it feels like there's more to the story...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What can you tell us about the Scions of the Canopy?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The tribespeople are very adventurous.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, kind of like us, then!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'm not so sure. You don't strike me as the type to enjoy danger.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The Scions of the Canopy are a bunch of thrill-seekers. They love extreme sports like rock climbing, rappelling, volcano parkour...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Or even bungee jumping without a rope while a Yumkasaur stands at the edge and uses its tongue to catch them. Sound like something you'd be interested in?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... that does sound different from our usual "adventures."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not doing any of that! She can just cheer you on from the sidelines!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: That's Wayna, the tribal chief. Let's head over to him.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Wayna's right over there. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Haah!

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Hya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, this place looks so different now... What happened here?
